prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app composition option, 1440x900 landscape
Primary request: Compose the first viewport of Bork, a polished dog-themed short-post social app and resume project, in a dark-first familiar social-feed world benchmarked against Bluesky friendliness and Twitter feed clarity without copying either brand. This is a composition study, not a new visual identity.
Scene/backdrop: continuous midnight-navy application canvas with charcoal raised surfaces, crisp cool-gray dividers, restrained sky-blue action color, warm dog portraits, and no white central column.
Subject: the real Bork experience: public feed, magic-link sign-in prompt, short dog posts, profiles, settings, theme control, and an authenticated composer when relevant. Show honest demo content only; no metrics, trends, follow recommendations, media posting, or unsupported features.
Style/medium: high-end modern social product UI, dark mode, friendly and technically credible, system-sans typography, precise spacing and state clarity.
Composition/framing: straight-on 1440x900 browser viewport. A compact left navigation rail with dog mark and wordmark takes about 18% width. One broad uninterrupted feed lane takes about 55%. A quiet right rail takes about 22% and contains only a concise “Built by Colton” project note and product stack proof, not social features. Composer is integrated at the top of the feed. Three text-only posts are visible. Mobile behavior is implied by clear units that can collapse.
Focal moment: the composer and newest post share one continuous reading lane; the BORK button is the only saturated control.
Lighting/mood: deep evening screen, calm, crisp, readable, subtly warm around portraits.
Color palette: #07111f canvas, #0d1b2a surfaces, #13263a raised surface, #d9e7f2 primary text, #8fa6b8 muted text, #2f9df4 action blue, #23374a dividers.
Materials/textures: flat app chrome with minute tonal elevation; no fake physical texture.
Text (verbatim where legible): “Bork”, “Feed”, “Profile”, “Settings”, “What’s happening, pup?”, “BORK”, “Public borks”, “Mabel”, “Found the sunny square. Claimed it.”, “Built by Colton”, “Next.js · TypeScript · tRPC · Supabase”.
Constraints: familiar social-feed affordances; dog personality in copy and content; dark mode across the entire viewport; one clear primary action; accessible contrast; no fake traction; no unsupported features; no copied logos.
Avoid: white feed column, gradients, glassmorphism, glow effects, bento cards, pill overload, excessive rounded containers, dashboard metrics, trends, follow suggestions, image-heavy posts, marketing hero, Twitter/X or Bluesky logo.
